subject: OrbisHealth PoC: private GPU pool throughput planning and network constraints

From: Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@orbishealth.com>

Date: 2026-10-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: OrbisHealth PoC: private GPU pool throughput planning and network constraints

Hi Priyom / Marissa / Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week — OrbisHealth is excited to move forward with a short private PoC in our GCP-hosted on-prem site. Before we lock in dates we'd like to align on throughput targets, expected latency, and any network constraints that might affect routing. High-level asks below: 

- Target sustained throughput: 1.2M tokens/day (mixed short/long requests; ~65% chat, 35% embeddings).
- 95th percentile latency target: <= 120ms for chat partial tokens; end-to-end generation for long documents (4-8k tokens) tolerates up to 800ms.
- Maintenance windows: we can provide a 2-hour nightly window (02:00–04:00 local) for upgrades, but prefer minimal cold starts for KV caches.
- Network: our site has a 10Gbps egress link, NAT in front of the GPU cluster, and strict egress IP allowlists for downstream services.

Attached is a short traffic profile (Orbis_traffic_profile.csv) and PoC requirements doc. Two specific questions for you:
1) What initial GPU pool size and instance mix would Redwood recommend to meet the sustained throughput while keeping tail latency targets?
2) How does Redwood's fallback routing to hosted capacity work if our private pool hits saturation? Any expected auth/telemetry differences?

Can we do a 30-minute call on Tuesday 10/21 to walk the traffic profile together? Mike from EdgeCloud (our systems integrator) will join.

Thanks,

Sarah Cho
Senior Platform Engineer, OrbisHealth

On Tue, Oct 20, 2026 at 09:12 AM Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@orbishealth.com> wrote:
> Hi Priyom / Marissa / Lauren,
> 
> Thanks again for the demo last week — OrbisHealth is excited to move forward with a short private PoC...

Sarah — thanks for the detail and the traffic CSV, that helped a lot. Quick summary of our read and a proposed starter configuration for the PoC. Happy to go into numbers on the call later today.

Assumptions (please confirm):
- Token composition roughly as you listed (65% chat, 35% embeddings).
- Average prompt+response length: chat: 350 tokens/session; embeddings requests ~512 tokens.
- Peak concurrent request bursts expected during 09:00–11:00 and 15:00–16:00 local.

Initial PoC sizing (conservative starter):
- GPU pool: 4 x A10G (8-GPU-equivalent throughput using sharing) presented as 4 machines with 1 model replica each.
- Expected sustained throughput: ~1.4M tokens/day headroom (with autoscaling headroom at +30% bursts).
- Latency: median chat token ~40–60ms; 95p partial token ~100–130ms depending on request size. For 4–8k gen paths expect up to 700–900ms at 95p in worst-case without aggressive KV priming.

Key configuration items:
- Autoscaler: conservative ramp up at 60% sustained CPU/GPU utilization, add one node per 2-minute throttle; burst policy to allow 1 node immediate scale for sudden spikes.
- KV cache warmup: recommend warmup on deploy and daily incremental priming run during the 02:00–04:00 window. Cold starts for long-docs will push the 95p latency as noted.
- Network: the 10Gbps egress is fine; we recommend a NAT IP pool dedicated to the Redwood runtime for allowlisting. If you enable private peering to Redwood control plane (recommended), there is maintained heartbeat + metrics through the control plane over a dedicated TLS channel.
- Fallback to hosted: seamless routing is possible per your policy. Auth is token-based; telemetry will include a routing tag (private->hosted) so logs show fallbacks. Note: requests routed to hosted may have different model variants (quantization/replicas) — expect slight variance in latency and output.

I've attached a starter capacity model (capacity_model_v1.xlsx) and a proposed topology sketch (network_topology.drawio). Proposed meeting: Tue 10/21 11:30am PT — please confirm.

Thanks — Priyom
Priyom Das
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: OrbisHealth PoC: private GPU pool throughput planning and network constraints

Follow-up after our call with Orbis and EdgeCloud (Mike). High-level decisions and action items for the PoC run: 

Decisions:
- Start PoC with Priyom's recommended 4x A10G baseline. This gives ~30% headroom for the 1.2M token/day stated target while keeping costs reasonable for Orbis.
- Autoscale policy: keep conservative ramp and enable burst policy for one immediate node allocation. Targets: scale up at 60% GPU util, scale down when below 30% over 5m.
- KV cache priming: run a scripted priming job in the 02:00–03:00 window with a lightweight dataset derived from Orbis traffic profile; schedule daily incremental priming afterwards.

Open questions / risks:
- Cold-start penalty for long-doc generation remains the biggest risk for meeting 95p in peak bursts. Marcus to prototype pre-warm strategies (partial KV checkpointing) and measure 95p improvements.
- Network egress allowlist: Orbis will provide final NAT IPs. We need to confirm control plane peering + an allowlist entry for our metrics endpoint.
- Fallback UX: we should document the observable differences users will see if requests route to hosted (slightly different model variant and potential higher token cost). Marissa to draft a fallback SLO note for the PoC run.

Action items (owners):
- Marcus Lin: prototype partial KV checkpointing and report delta in 95p for 4k/8k token paths by 2026-11-02.
- Priyom Das: finalize capacity spreadsheet and push a v1 runbook with scaling knobs to the Confluence page (link below) by 10/27.
- Marissa Cole: draft fallback SLO/communication note and include cost delta estimates by 10/28.
- Sarah / EdgeCloud: confirm NAT IPs and maintenance blackout windows by 10/27.

Relevant links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/GPUPool-ORBH-POC

Thanks everyone — sound plan and reasonable headroom for the PoC.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Principal Product Manager, Private Deployments, Redwood Inference
